subject: Post-demo: procurement & hosting options — PO vs card, commit vs on-demand
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia.barnes@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: procurement & hosting options — PO vs card, commit vs on-demand

Hi Olivia — thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can align pricing and procurement paperwork with Acme Health's buying rules.

Recap (30-min demo):
- Covered Redwood hosted API and Dedicated pools; touched on Private deployment for regulated workloads.
- Showed typical latency/cost tradeoffs and commit discounts for reserved capacity.

Clarifying questions to help procurement:
1) Purchase instrument: do you need a PO for all purchases or only for annual commits beyond a threshold? (We often see PO required for $15k+ ARR.)
2) Billing path: are you open to marketplace (GCP/AWS) purchase to centralize vendor management, or do you prefer a direct vendor invoice/credit card?
3) Hosting preference: talk to legal/regulatory — will Acme allow hosted (SaaS) for this workload or is Dedicated/Private required?
4) Timeline: who on your side will own the SOW/PO execution and what's the expected procurement window?

Attached: pricing_options_Q3_v2.pdf — high-level compare: hosted (on-demand), hosted (commit), Dedicated (6/12 mo commit), Private (quote).

Next steps I suggest: you tell us the preferred buying lane (PO on direct invoice, marketplace, or card) and we’ll return a short procurement checklist + pricing for the two most likely paths. If you prefer, we can also prepare a 6-month dedicated commit quote vs on-demand cost projection.

Thanks — Karthik

--

Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement & hosting options — PO vs card, commit vs on-demand

Karthik — appreciate the recap and the pricing doc. A few notes from Procurement/IT: 

1) Purchase instrument: our standard is PO for any vendor spend that will be invoiced monthly and exceeds $12k committed ARR. For short pilot/integration work (<$5k) our teams sometimes use a corporate card. So PO is likely for the scenario you outlined if we go above pilot.

2) Marketplace: Acme prefers marketplace purchases when possible because Finance consolidates vendor spend that way. We are on GCP Marketplace and prefer vendors to support that lane.

3) Hosting: clinical workloads with PHI will require Private or a Dedicated instance behind our VPC; non-PHI dev/prod can live on hosted. We need to validate data residency controls and SOC2 reports.

4) Security evidence: please share SOC2 type II and high-level network diagram. Our security team (Samir) will need to review.

5) Discounts/commits: Procurement will evaluate a 6- or 12-month committed spend if the discount and SLA justify it; otherwise we'll default to on-demand with usage caps.

If you can send a concise procurement checklist (SOW, PO template, lead time for Private/Dedicated provisioning, and billing path options including marketplace), I’ll route it to Finance and Samir. Our timeline: we aim to have purchase path decided within 2–3 weeks if the quotes and docs are available.

Thanks,
Olivia

--
Olivia Barnes
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Health
olivia.barnes@acmehealth.com | +1 (617) 555-4789

Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: procurement & hosting options — PO vs card, commit vs on-demand

Karthik — forwarding Olivia's procurement notes. Below are proposed alignments we can present to Acme: 

Option A — Hosted (managed API)
- Best for quick pilot and dev testing; low lead time; supports marketplace listing for consolidated billing.
- Pricing: on-demand per token or monthly committed spend for lower unit cost.
- Good when no PHI in production.

Option B — Dedicated (Redwood Dedicated pool)
- Predictable throughput, can be deployed in customer region; acceptable if Acme wants isolation but still wants Redwood-managed infra.
- Commit options: 6- or 12-month reserved capacity with tiered discounts (we typically offer 15% for 6mo, 25% for 12mo at commit thresholds).
- Billing supports PO/direct invoice; marketplace depends on cloud partner capabilities.

Option C — Private (VPC/On-prem)
- For PHI/regulatory: Private deployment with customer-managed network and KMS integration.
- Longer lead time, quoted pricing, enterprise contract. PO expected.

Ask for product: can we validate marketplace listing availability for GCP (yes/no) and estimated lead time to provision a Dedicated instance in us-east-1? Marcus — can you confirm SLA/lead times and attach SOC2 link?

I’ll draft a 1-page procurement checklist and a short commit vs on-demand run-rate comparison to send back to Olivia.

Thanks — Monica

--
Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement & hosting options — PO vs card, commit vs on-demand

Olivia — thanks, that is very helpful and aligns with what we expected. Below is a condensed procurement checklist and two concrete commercial paths for Acme to evaluate. I’ve attached the checklist and a short cost comparison.

Procurement checklist (one-pager attached):
- SOC2 Type II report (link below) — Security review by Samir.
- SOW template + statement of work scope for pilot/production.
- PO template or credit card option for pilot.
- Marketplace listing confirmation (GCP) or vendor invoice flow.
- Lead times: Hosted = immediate; Dedicated = ~2–3 weeks post-SOW; Private = quoted (6+ weeks typical).

Commercial paths:
1) Marketplace / Hosted (fastest)
- Pilot on hosted, purchase via GCP Marketplace (Finance consolidation).
- Move to committed hosted monthly credits if usage grows.

2) PO + Dedicated Commit (predictable cost)
- 6- or 12-month reserved capacity with invoice/PO billing.
- We can model a 6-month commit vs on-demand run-rate — Monica attached the projection.

Next steps — pick 1 path you’d like a formal quote for and we’ll:
- Return a DocuSign-ready quote + SOW for PO path (if chosen).
- Share Marketplace SKU and purchase instructions if GCP path chosen.
- Provide SOC2 and network diagram for Samir’s review.

Timeline: if you confirm preferred path by Aug 29 we can have a PO-ready doc or marketplace instructions back within 5 business days.

Attachments: procurement_checklist.docx, pricing_options_Q3_v2.pdf (original)
